title.narrative: SIWI World Water Week and International Policy

description.narrative:
The Stockholm International Water Institute, SIWI, works globally to change how water is understood, valued and managed. As advocates and advisors, we show how improved water governance is key to a fairer, more prosperous, and resilient future.
SIWI is a not-for-profit institute with a wide range of expertise in water governance – from sanitation and water resources management to water diplomacy. We create knowledge, develop capacity, and offer policy advice to countries, communities, and companies.
Almost all of humanity’s most pressing challenges, from climate change to poverty, are closely linked to water. Through our work, we contribute to poverty reduction, climate resilience, healthy ecosystems, and more prosperous and inclusive societies. Improving water governance is fundamental to achieving the 2030 Agenda on Sustainable Development.
Thanks to our multi-disciplinary approach, we can strengthen policy and extend reach via our international programmes, projects, and multi-stakeholder platforms. These activities allow us to innovate and develop applied knowledge and tools for water governance.
SIWI organizes the world’s leading water conference, World Water Week, and awards the prestigious Stockholm Water Prize. We also empower young people to solve water issues through the international competition Stockholm Junior Water Prize.

2021 Q2: 1. Climate Adaptation Summit in January, SIWI provided speakers as well as communicated around the event, e.g. with blog posts (over 100 reads), videos (over 500 views), and social media posts.
2.Work has begun on planning for a Water Pavilion at COP26, gathering interest from the water community and providing unprecedented visibility for water in the climate sphere.
3.SIWI has submitted written input to the 2021 HLPF theme, as well as input to the NGO Major Group Position Paper, emphasising the importance of water for combatting covid-19 and building resilience.
4.Procurement of a consultant started in Q1, and from Q2 onwards a New York-based consultant will support the implementation of activities in connection to UN-Water and looking ahead to UNGA and the UN Food Systems Summit.
2021 Q3: 1. Supporting and contributing to the Dushanbe Int Conference for MTR (finalizing official documents of the conference, reshaping the sessions SIWI is involved in), participation in the Int Advisory committee
2. SIWI has been the lead organization for the arrangement of the Water Pavilion in the blue zone of COP26 in Glasgow. In this effort, SIWI has cooperated with 26 other organizations and UN agencies, as well as the governments of the Netherlands, Tajikistan, Germany, Scotland and the UK. Together with the partner organizations, SIWI has raised 365,634 euros to fund the costs associated with the build and space rental of the pavilion as well as communications efforts. With the help from three communications agencies, SIWI has hosted communications workshops with the partner organizations to develop joint key messages, a communications toolkit, a visual approach including a joint logo, and a webpage. Furthermore, SIWI has led the effort to ensure a hybrid pavilion, contracting Pathable to host virtual events. Similarly, SIWI has made sure that all events will be available free of charge or registration requirements, to ensure the Water Pavilion to be as inclusive as possible. According to the same logic, SIWI has also undertaken a specific outreach project to connect with stakeholders in the global south.
The Water Pavilion received about 170 expressions of interest from event organizers. The Water Pavilion is hosting 87 events throughout the COP conference, that are all aligned with the topics negotiated by the Parties and with a clear connection to water.
3. Inputting and influencing the political ministerial declaration of HLPF to ensure that water is mentioned, organization of a side event with FWP on resilient water management for implementing 2030 Agenda, contribution to UN water GAF special event, dedicated communication tools.
4. SIWI’s consultant attended the processes and summits for HLPF, UNFCCC Bonn Intersessionals, Food System Summit, the Energy Summit as well as the High-level Ocean event- influencing strategy developed for various calls to highlight water in topline messaging. For example, the FSS, interventions for Action Areas were submitted with partners CGIAR and IWMI to build on the learnings that are arising on water and food systems in national and regional dialogues.
Through SIWI's engagement and observer status, we continued to unpack the major water challenges and linkages to food systems highlighting cross-cutting solutions to jointly improve food systems and water security.
The recommendations and outcomes put forward were that the United Nations Food Security Summit (UNFSS) should consider including: 1) Strengthening efforts to retain water-based ecosystems and their functions; 2) Improving agricultural water management for better diets for all; 3) Reducing water and food losses beyond the farmgate; 4) Coordinating water with nutrition and health interventions; 5) Increasing the environmental sustainability of food systems; 6) Explicitly addressing social inequities in water-nutrition linkages; and 7) Improving data quality and monitoring for water-food system linkages, drawing on innovations in information and communications technology (ICT).
Similar to the interventions submitted to the FSS, all of these summaries and analyses below can influence thematic opportunities to tie global processes to the 2023 Midterm Review. See attached document.

description.narrative:
High-Level Dialogue arranged during WWW 2019: Now branded as "High Level Panel", the concept note for the HLP on "Strengthening Synergies, Accelerating Action" was co-developed by SIWI and GoN, including the selection of the keynote speaker (Ms. Kitty van der Heijden) and the panelists. The event will be pre-recorded in mid-August and will be aired on 23 August during World Water Week.
High-Level Dialogue arranged during WWW 2021: The HLD was very successful in bringing together world leading experts working with different aspects of development, and managed to identify new and innovative synergies between the different stakeholders and their respective fields.
Below follows an in-detail description of the even:
The HLD was introduced by SIWI’s Executive Director, Torgny Holmgren. This was followed by a scene-setter by Kitty van der Heijden the Director-General for International Cooperation at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands.
The first panel covered internationals agendas and their interrelationship with water. It was moderated by Henk Ovink, the Special Envoy for International Water Affairs of the Netherlands. The panel was composed of Nigel Topping, UNFCCC COP26 High-Level Champion for Global Climate Action of the UK; Agnes Kalibata, the UN Secretary General’s Special Envoy to the 2021 Food Systems Summit; and Maria Neira, Director of the Department of Public Health and Environment at the World Health Organization.
The second panel consisted of different water professionals and was moderated by Jennifer Jun, Senior Manager for International Policy at SIWI. The panel included Kelly Ann Naylor, Vice-Chair for UN-Water; Thomas Stratenwerth, Working Group Leader at the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMU) of Germany; Japheth Habinshuti, Chief Resilience Officer at the City of Kigali; and Lindsey Blodgétt, Youth Representative at the Water and Climate Coalition.
The two panels were summarized in a digital sketch and Jennifer Jun closed the session.
Two central recommendations coming out of the HLD are presented below:
First, a functioning climate, health system, and agriculture are all interdependent on a water cycle in balance. For instance, if there is water stress due to climate change, people are likely to lack sanitation facilities which increases the transmission of diseases. Thus, policy must provide a comprehensive response to all global challenges.
Second, advancing water goals means advancing the goals on climate action, food security and human health. Water is a pure synergy, by building strong water management structures and implementing WASH, we build strong and resilient responses to climate change and health crises as well as secure the access of food to all.
151 people registered to the HLD, of which 123 attended the live stream of the event. Importantly, the recording of the HLD was available on the World Water Week platform after its streaming, why it is likely that even more people have watched it.
Improved registration process, especially for returning participants.
Individual team members are developing strong networks, capacity and can leverage the overall Dutch engagement at World Water Week.

Joint messages from the Advisory Committee for World Water Week: Key messages were revised several times and will aim for adoption at the 17 August Advisory Committee members meeting. In the meantime, SIWI will incorporate key messages in the Opening and Closing Plenaries of World Water Week as well as the High Level Panel on Strengthening Synergies.
2021: Advisory Committee meeting in Q1 left input to messages, which are currently being drafted in preparation for adoption in Q2.. Messages adopted prior to WWW2021 and promoted during the plenaries, HLD session and in different communication channels (social media, articles, blogs,…)

title.narrative: UN Water convened Food System Dialogue

SIWI contributed to the UN Water convened Food System Dialogue in April 2021 through the NY consultant, as well conduct bilateral meetings on water's contribution to the UNFSSS process with IWMI and UN-Water's Leanne Burney.
Position Paper in cooperation with NGO Major Group

SIWI's input into the NGO Major Group Position Paper, emphasising the importance of water for combatting covid-19 and building resilience, were incorporated. The Q3 report will provide update on the final report (https://www.ngomg.org/reports).
Input provided on water-energy linkages in the Stakeholders Thematic E-Consultation ahead of the autumn's UN High-Level Dialogue on Energy.
Water & Climate Pavilion in the Blue Zone of COP26

Advanced planning for Water & Climate Pavilion in the Blue Zone of COP26, leading planing calls biweekly with 20+ partners and creating common vision and strategy for strengthening visibility for water among climate decisionmakers. Official application for the Blue Zone submitted.
